source "https://rubygems.org"
git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

# Architecture

## Starting point

Margin Notes is a reading-notebook application. Implemented so far:

- A reader (`User`) signs in with email and password through `has_secure_password`.
  `SessionsController` stores only the user ID in the Rails session.
  `ApplicationController#require_sign_in` protects the application's other
  controllers, but not Rails' Active Storage controllers.
- A reader owns `Notebook`s, and each `Note` belongs to one notebook. A note's
  owner is its notebook's owner, so `User#notes` (through notebooks) is the
  authorized note scope. There is no separate `user_id` on notes.
- `NotesController#index` serves `/notes` and its `/journal` alias. It lists the
  reader's notes newest first with an ID tie-breaker, and supports title search
  and notebook and status filters. `show` renders one note's rich body.
- Pagy 8.6.3 paginates that filtered list after ordering, 10 notes per page by
  default. The search form offers 5, 10, 25, or 50 as the `per_page` URL
  parameter. Larger requested sizes are capped at 50. Next and previous links keep
  the filters and page size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric page shows the
  first page, and a page past the end shows the last page. The form never sends
  an invalid size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric `per_page` in a URL is
  not handled, and Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`.
- A note's body is Action Text (`has_rich_text :body`), edited with Trix.
  Attachments are Active Storage blobs on the local Disk service. `Note` rejects
  saves that embed a blob over 1 MB. Direct uploads store blobs before this
  validation, without a size limit. Rejected or abandoned uploads remain
  unattached, and nothing purges them. No image processor is installed, so images
  use the original blobs, not variants. A migration converted existing plain-text
  bodies to escaped rich text.
- Action Text sanitizes rich text when it renders. The
  [Action Text initializer](config/initializers/action_text.rb) adds
  `details`/`summary` to the default allowlist for collapsible excerpts. Trix
  does not support those elements. Stored excerpts render as collapsible content,
  but saving them through the editor permanently flattens that structure, even
  when only tags or highlight change.
- Note tags are a JSON array in a text column, entered as a comma-separated
  list (`Note#tag_list`). The highlight color is `color` in the `settings` jsonb
  column, which the form edits as `highlight_color`.
- `NotebooksController#edit`/`update` are notebook settings. The slug is derived
  from the name on creation and is read-only afterward (`attr_readonly`). The
  settings form resubmits it unchanged. The export heading is stored in the
  serialized `preferences` hash. Markdown exports use both.
- A reader imports a CSV into one owned notebook. `ImportPreviewsController`
  reads the upload and renders a preview without saving. The preview page sends
  the CSV text back in a hidden field, and `ImportsController#create` reads and
  validates it again rather than trusting the preview. `Import#apply` saves the
  import and each row's note in one transaction. If any row cannot be saved,
  nothing from the batch remains. The receipt page and its CSV download list
  each imported note's title and DOI. Submitting the same preview twice creates
  two imports.
- `Import` accepts one format: UTF-8 CSV with the header row
  `title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch`, at most 100 notes and 100 KB.
  Only the title is required. Previews identify rows by their source line, so a
  quoted multi-line body keeps the line where its row starts. Body HTML takes the
  same Action Text assignment and render-time sanitization as the editor.
- A `Citation` is identified by its DOI, the table's `doi` primary key, and is
  shared by every reader who cites it. A DOI is stored as given apart from
  surrounding whitespace, so case variants are different citations. Rows in one
  import share a new citation. Two simultaneous imports that introduce the same
  new DOI can conflict; the losing request fails with a server error and saves
  nothing. A reader's annotation and optional reminder epoch belong to the note,
  not the citation. Annotations are plain text in both the preview and note page;
  line breaks are preserved on the note page, but markup is displayed literally.
  Applying an import does not schedule its reminders; the reader schedules each
  one from its note.
- A reader can also enter a DOI on the note form (`Note#doi=`), which cites the
  shared citation with that exact, trimmed DOI or creates it.
- A reader requests metadata for the citation on one of their notes with
  `CitationEnrichmentsController#create`, nested under the note. It resolves the
  note through `current_user.notes`, so another reader's note, or a note without
  a DOI, is a 404. `Citation#request_enrichment` marks the citation pending and
  queues `CitationEnrichmentJob`, unless a request is already pending. The job
  calls `Citation#enrich`, which stores the provider's title and source URL and
  marks the citation completed, or records a failure message. Metadata and
  status belong to the shared citation, so every note citing the DOI shows them.
  The note page shows the state; it does not update itself while pending.
- `Citation::Provider` is the HTTP client for the metadata provider. It reads
  its URL and basic-auth credentials from [config/secrets.yml](config/secrets.yml)
  through `Rails.application.secrets`; that file reads them from the environment.
  Faraday retries a GET once on 503. A 401, 403, or 404, or a response without a
  title and an http(s) URL, fails the enrichment at once. A 429 or 5xx, timeout,
  or connection failure raises `Citation::Provider::Unavailable`. The job retries
  that with `retry_on`, three attempts in all at exponentially longer waits, then
  records the failure instead of passing the error to Sidekiq's own retries. A
  persistently unavailable provider therefore receives at most six requests per
  enrichment request. A job that fails for another reason uses Sidekiq's retries
  and leaves the citation pending meanwhile.
- [bin/citation-provider](bin/citation-provider) is a deterministic local stand-in
  for the provider, used for development and demonstrations. No real provider or
  credentials are configured.
- A reader exports an owned notebook as Markdown from its exports page
  (`ExportsController`, nested under the notebook). `Notebook#request_export`
  saves a queued `Export`, then queues the native Sidekiq job `ExportJob` and
  stores its job ID, which the page shows. The export is committed before the
  job is queued so the worker can always load it. If Redis refuses the job, the
  export is removed and the request fails. Each request creates a new export.
- `Export#generate`, run by the worker, marks the export working with the
  notebook's note count, then writes the notes oldest first (creation time, then
  ID). The file starts with the notebook's export heading, or its name when none
  is set. Each note is a second-level heading with its title on one line,
  followed by its body as Action Text plain text. Markdown characters are not
  escaped. Progress is saved after each note. A retried job starts again from
  the first note. There is no failed state: while Sidekiq retries a failing job,
  the export shows as working and the reader can cancel it.
- Cancelling (`ExportCancellationsController`) sets a queued or working export's
  persisted status to cancelled under its row lock. The worker checks that status
  before each note and before completing, then stops and keeps no file. Completed
  and cancelled exports cannot be cancelled.
- The worker uploads the file to Active Storage (`<slug>.md`) before marking the
  export completed, so a completed export always has a file. It can be downloaded
  for 24 hours (`Export::AVAILABLE_FOR`). `ExportDownloadsController` resolves the
  export through the reader's notebook, so another reader's export is a 404, and
  checks `Export#downloadable?` on every request before any conditional response.
  An expired, cancelled, or unfinished export redirects to the exports page. The
  file is sent by the application, never by an Active Storage URL, with an ETag
  and Last-Modified from the stored file and `private, must-revalidate`.
  A failed upload can leave an unattached blob row without a stored file. Nothing
  cleans up those rows, and each failed retry can leave another one.
- The exports page caches each completed export's availability indicator as a
  fragment that expires at the export's deadline. The download action does not
  read that cache. The page does not update itself while an export is queued or
  working. Nothing purges expired files; they remain in storage.
- A notebook's activity page (`ActivityReportsController#show`, nested under the
  notebook and linked from the notebooks list) shows how many of its notes were
  created on each UTC date, newest date first. It is read-only and resolves the
  notebook through `current_user.notebooks`, so another reader's notebook is a
  404. `Notebook#daily_note_counts` groups the notes by `DATE(created_at)` in
  PostgreSQL and reads the rows with a raw `select_rows`, which returns each date
  as ISO 8601 text; the method parses it with `Date.iso8601`. Every status counts,
  and dates without notes are omitted. The report is derived from the notes that
  exist when it is requested, not an activity log: deleting a note lowers its
  date's count, and nothing records past counts.
- Each reader has a time zone (`User#time_zone`, UTC by default), chosen on the
  account settings page (`AccountsController`). Reminder times use it. Digests
  follow UTC days, and other pages still show times in UTC.
- A note's reminder is its `reminder_epoch`, a time in seconds since 1970, set by
  an import or by the reader. `RemindersController#create`, nested under the
  note, reads a date and time the reader entered in their time zone
  (`User#local_time`), or, with none, uses the stored time. `Note#schedule_reminder`
  queues `NoteReminderJob` for that time with `set(wait_until:)` and stores the
  job's ID, under the note's row lock, so a failed enqueue keeps the earlier
  reminder. A local time that does not exist because of a daylight saving change
  moves forward, and an ambiguous one takes its first occurrence. A time in the
  past is sent as soon as a worker runs the job.
- Scheduling again, or postponing (`ReminderPostponementsController`), replaces the
  reminder. Earlier jobs stay in Sidekiq's schedule, but send nothing: when a job
  runs, `Note#send_reminder` takes the row lock and emails the reader only if its
  job ID is still the note's and the reminder has not been sent, then records
  `reminder_sent_at`. The note page shows whether a reminder is imported but not
  scheduled, scheduled, or sent. A job that fails after the email is written can
  send it again when Sidekiq retries it.
- Postponing moves the reminder 24 elapsed hours later. The note page previews
  that time as `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`, which keeps the reminder's UTC
  offset. Across a daylight saving change the preview shows the right instant,
  but at a different offset and wall-clock time from the postponed reminder.
- A reader requests a digest of their ready notes from the notes page
  (`DigestsController`). `User#request_digest` reserves the reader's ID in a
  Redis set for the request's UTC date
  (`digest_requests:YYYY-MM-DD`, kept for two days) and queues `DigestJob` with
  the reader, the request time in the reader's zone, and the share of their notes
  that are ready, as a `BigDecimal`. A reader whose ID is already in the day's set
  is told the digest was already requested. If the job cannot be queued, the
  reservation is removed and the error raised, so the request fails and can be
  repeated. The reservation prevents repeated requests, not repeated emails:
  Sidekiq can run a job more than once. Each request logs redis-rb's deprecation
  warning for a single-member `sadd`, and Sidekiq warns that the job's arguments
  are not native JSON types, because of the `BigDecimal`.
- Sidekiq stores the job's arguments as JSON. Active Job 7.0 sends the request
  time with its UTC offset but deserializes it in the worker's zone, UTC, and the
  completion arrives as a decimal string such as `"0.6667"`. `DigestMailer` lists
  the reader's ready notes last updated during that UTC day, and dates the digest
  by it. The content day matches the reservation's day, even near local midnight.
  A digest is a snapshot when its job runs; notes updated afterward are not sent
  in a second digest for that UTC day.
- The mailers write plain-text email. Development writes each recipient's email
  to `tmp/mails` (Action Mailer's file delivery); tests use the `:test` delivery
  method. Production has no delivery method or link host configured.
- Active Storage serves blobs through signed URLs from its own controllers. Those
  URLs are not checked against the signed-in reader. The embedded blob redirect
  URLs do not expire, although the Disk-service URLs they redirect to do.
  The direct-upload controller checks CSRF, not sign-in; the public sign-in page
  supplies a CSRF token to anonymous clients. This sample has no private-file
  access policy or upload-abuse protection for a public deployment.

These conventions guide further features without prescribing a schema in advance.

The initial runtime is Ruby 3.3.6 and Rails 7.0.8.7 with Rails 7.0 defaults.
[Gemfile](Gemfile), [Gemfile.lock](Gemfile.lock), [.ruby-version](.ruby-version), and
[config/application.rb](config/application.rb) are the executable sources of truth.

- PostgreSQL is the application database. Use Active Record and migrations for
  application-owned records, constraints, indexes, and transactions.
- ERB renders HTML. The generated app includes Sprockets, importmap, Turbo, and
  Stimulus. Jbuilder is available for requested JSON representations, but an HTML
  feature does not automatically need a JSON API.
- Rails includes the mailer, job, storage, and cable frameworks. Their presence
  does not mean broadcasts are implemented features. Email is sent only for
  reminders and digests, and is not delivered outside development's files. File
  uploads exist only as rich-text attachments.
- Active Job uses Sidekiq 6.5 as its adapter outside tests, so queued jobs are
  kept in Redis (`REDIS_URL`, by default `redis://localhost:6379`) and run in a
  separate `bundle exec sidekiq` process. Tests use Active Job's test adapter.
  `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job rather than an Active Job, so its job ID can
  be shown. Sidekiq stores its arguments as JSON, and it uses Sidekiq's default
  retries.
- Action Text 7.0.8.7 bundles Trix 1.3.4. That version cannot load saved HTML
  that has attributes, such as links or attachments, so the layout loads Trix
  1.3.5 from `vendor/javascript` as a classic script. Trix 1.x is not an ES
  module, so it is not in the import map. `@rails/actiontext` is.
  The vendored build comes from the [Trix 1.3.5 release](https://github.com/basecamp/trix/tree/1.3.5)
  and includes its [MIT license](vendor/javascript/trix-1.3.5.LICENSE).
- Orb setup starts PostgreSQL and Redis. Redis holds Sidekiq's queues and the
  digest reservations; it is not an application cache. The generated production
  cable configuration names Redis. That configuration is not a verified deployment.

## Prefer Rails objects with clear responsibilities

Use the framework's ordinary directories and interfaces:

| Responsibility | Home |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP verbs, paths, and resource nesting | `config/routes.rb` |
| Parameter selection, authorized lookup, response negotiation | `app/controllers/` |
| Persistent state and domain operations | `app/models/` |
| A cohesive capability of one model | A namespace beneath `app/models/` |
| Behavior genuinely shared across models | `app/models/concerns/` |
| HTML, Turbo stream, and JSON representations | `app/views/` |
| Presentation helpers | `app/helpers/` |
| Browser interaction around rendered HTML | `app/javascript/controllers/` |
| Background execution and retry boundary | `app/jobs/` |
| Mail composition | `app/mailers/` and its views |

A controller can call Active Record directly for a simple save. A multi-step
domain transition belongs behind a meaningful model method, not a sequence of
unrelated updates in the controller. Use a plain Ruby object or Active Model when
an operation needs its own object but no database table. Do not introduce a
mandatory service, repository, presenter, or command layer between every pair of
Rails objects.

Fizzy models closing a card as a singular closure resource. Its controller calls
`Card#close`, and `Card::Closeable` owns the association, predicates, and transaction.
The [closure sources](docs/references/fizzy.md#card-closure) illustrate a resource
boundary and a domain method, not a requirement to add cards to Margin Notes.

## Model resources, not collections of verbs

Use the conventional REST actions, including `new` and `edit` for HTML forms.
When a new operation does not fit an existing resource, look for the resource it
creates, updates, or removes before adding a custom action. Keep nesting shallow
enough that the parent conveys ownership rather than reproducing the whole schema.

Use route helpers in views and responses. Controllers choose the representation.
Models do not construct controller responses or reach into request parameters.

## Keep data ownership and effects explicit

- PostgreSQL owns durable application facts. Derive a value from those facts
  unless storing it solves a demonstrated query, history, or concurrency need.
- Put invariants used outside HTTP in the domain model. Add database constraints
  when integrity must also hold across concurrent requests and non-model writes.
- Keep related database writes in one transaction. Do not assume it can undo a
  remote request, an email, or a job already sent to another system.
- Jobs should delegate to domain behavior and carry the identifiers or context
  they need. Decide retries, duplicate delivery, and transaction timing when a
  real background feature is introduced, rather than adding a queue preemptively.
- Keep network clients at visible boundaries. Preserve failure information and
  distinguish a legitimate empty response from a failed operation.

Fizzy's [comment example](docs/references/fizzy.md#comments) enforces comment
eligibility in both the model and the controller. Callers outside HTTP must obey
the same rule.

## Authorization is not presentation

Define ownership and the authorized lookup scope together. Resolve records
through the signed-in reader: `current_user.notebooks` and `current_user.notes`.
Direct lookups outside that scope raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is
a 404 in production. A submitted `notebook_id` is resolved through
`current_user.notebooks.find_by`, never assigned directly. A missing or foreign
notebook fails validation and renders the form with 422, without saving the note.
Resolve nested records through their authorized parent. Neither an unguessable ID
nor a hidden or disabled button grants or checks permission.

Keep actor-dependent decisions explicit in domain APIs and reusable rendering.
If request-local state is introduced, set and reset it at the request boundary.
Jobs, mailers, and tests must not rely on a previous request having populated it.
Do not adopt a tenancy or identity scheme solely because a reference application
uses one.

## Render on the server, enhance in the browser

Use HTML forms and links for their native semantics. Turbo handles navigation,
frames, and targeted replacements. Stimulus supplies local interaction that HTML
does not provide. Keep persistence and authorization on the server, not in a
second client-side model of the domain.

Partials take the resources and presentation inputs they need. A template may
compose several resources. A reusable partial should not depend on a particular
controller's incidental instance variables or on undeclared request context.
See the [view guide](docs/guides/views.md) for HTML, accessibility, Turbo, and JSON.

## Optimize the actual representation

Start with correct queries and clear response contracts. Filter and order before
pagination. Use a stable tie-breaker where page membership must be deterministic.
Load the associations that the rendered representation uses rather than adding
a universal preload list to every request.

Define cache keys and invalidation rules before introducing caching. Include
permissions, locale, and related-record changes when they affect the output, or
keep those parts outside the shared fragment. The
[board example](docs/references/fizzy.md#boards-and-caching) illustrates why a
warm cache must be tested with another viewer, not just the same request twice.

## Scope and reference boundaries

The [public examples](docs/references/fizzy.md) are evidence for design ideas, not
a compatible application template. Their Ruby, Rails, database adapters, asset
pipeline, editors, and helper libraries differ from this repository. Use the
locked local APIs, and introduce new infrastructure only for a requested feature.

As features land, document their ownership and invariants here. Keep detailed
layer practices in the [model](docs/guides/models.md),
[controller](docs/guides/controllers.md), and [view](docs/guides/views.md) guides,
and verification rules in [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).
# Testing

## Test the contract at its boundary

Use Rails' Minitest integration with real application objects and the test
PostgreSQL database. Exercise the route, controller, model, and rendering stack
for HTTP behavior. When needed, substitute a controlled response at an external
boundary. Do not stub the domain behavior under test.

Choose the smallest boundary that can catch the likely mistake:

| Contract | Test |
| --- | --- |
| A domain decision, transition, or query | `ActiveSupport::TestCase` in `test/models/` |
| Routing, permissions, persistence, HTML, Turbo, or JSON | `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` in `test/controllers/` |
| A workflow across endpoints | An integration test in `test/integration/` |
| Browser execution, focus, navigation, or JavaScript interaction | `ApplicationSystemTestCase` in `test/system/` |
| Scheduling, delivery, and job-specific failure behavior | Rails job and mailer test helpers, usually in the request test that queues the job |

Do not add a separate test for every method. Prefer assertions that would survive
an internal refactor. A useful regression test fails for a plausible wrong
implementation, not just a syntax error.

## Commands and current configuration

Use only a disposable test database. Rails may create, reload, or replace its
data. Never point test configuration at development data you need to keep, a
shared environment, or production.

Run commands from the repository root with the pinned Ruby active:

```sh
bundle check
bin/rails zeitwerk:check
bin/rails test
bin/rails test:system
```

`bin/rails test` does not include system tests. The generated
[system test base](test/application_system_test_case.rb) uses Selenium with Chrome,
not headless Chrome. Until that configuration changes, system tests require a
display and a suitable browser and driver.

For focused feedback, run a test directory:

```sh
bin/rails test test/controllers
bin/rails test test/models
```

To run one file, pass its path to `bin/rails test`. Append `:LINE` to that path to
select a test.

The Gemfile keeps Minitest on 5.x because Rails 7.0's test runner fails under
Minitest 6. No RuboCop, security-audit command, or `bin/ci` is configured.

[test/test_helper.rb](test/test_helper.rb) loads all fixtures and configures
processor-count parallel workers.

The [test environment](config/environments/test.rb) disables caching and raises
application exceptions. For error-response or cache tests, set the required mode
explicitly and restore it afterward. Do not assume production behavior. The mail
delivery method is `:test`.

## Make scenarios distinguish the right behavior

- Name the domain fact or user outcome: a rejected edit leaves the body unchanged,
  not merely that an update action runs.
- Keep arrangement, action, and assertions recognizable. Share setup only for
  facts every test in that group needs. Do not hide the decisive input in a helper.
- Establish meaningful preconditions when the operation could otherwise be a
  no-op. Reload records when checking what was persisted.
- Use asymmetric values and contrasting records. A permission test needs another
  user's record. A filter needs both an included and an excluded candidate.
- Derive expected results independently. Do not call the production scope or
  serializer to compute the value the same scope or serializer should return.
- Assert order only where ordering is promised. For membership, include/exclude
  assertions can express the rule better than an exact count of unrelated fixtures.
  Assert total counts when pagination, duplicates, or filtering totals are contractual.
- Test both a successful result and the relevant failure or boundary. A denial

      def determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm:, executions:, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT)
        jitter = jitter == JITTER_DEFAULT ? self.class.retry_jitter : (jitter || 0.0)

        case seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
        when  :polynomially_longer
          # This delay uses a polynomial backoff strategy, which was previously misnamed as exponential
          delay = executions**4
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter + 2
        when ActiveSupport::Duration, Integer
          delay = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm.to_i
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter
        when Proc
          algorithm = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
          algorithm.call(executions)
        else
          raise "Couldn't determine a delay based on #{seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm.inspect}"
        end

        if self.class.enqueue_after_transaction_commit

# frozen_string_literal: true

gem "sidekiq", ">= 4.1.0"
require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Sidekiq adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Simple, efficient background processing for Ruby. Sidekiq uses threads to
    # handle many jobs at the same time in the same process. It does not
    # require \Rails but will integrate tightly with it to make background
    # processing dead simple.
    #
    # Read more about Sidekiq {here}[http://sidekiq.org].
    #
    # To use Sidekiq set the queue_adapter config to +:sidekiq+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
    class SidekiqAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def initialize(*) # :nodoc:
        @stopping = false

        Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end

        Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end
      end

      def check_adapter
        ActiveJob.deprecator.warn <<~MSG.squish
          The built-in `sidekiq` adapter is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2.
          Please upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
        MSG
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name
        ).perform_async(job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name,
        ).perform_at(timestamp, job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_all(jobs) # :nodoc:
        enqueued_count = 0
        jobs.group_by(&:class).each do |job_class, same_class_jobs|
          same_class_jobs.group_by(&:queue_name).each do |queue, same_class_and_queue_jobs|
            immediate_jobs, scheduled_jobs = same_class_and_queue_jobs.partition { |job| job.scheduled_at.nil? }

            if immediate_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => immediate_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end

            if scheduled_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
                "at" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| job.scheduled_at&.to_f }
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end
          end
        end
        enqueued_count
      end

      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        include Sidekiq::Worker

        def perform(job_data)
          Base.execute job_data.merge("provider_job_id" => jid)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

    # Returns an instance of DateTime with the timezone's UTC offset

    #   Time.current.in_time_zone('Hawaii').to_datetime   # => Mon, 17 Aug 2015 16:32:20 -1000
    def to_datetime
      @to_datetime ||= utc.to_datetime.new_offset(Rational(utc_offset, 86_400))
    end

    # Returns an instance of +Time+, either with the same timezone as +self+,
    # with the same UTC offset as +self+ or in the local system timezone
    # depending on the setting of +ActiveSupport.to_time_preserves_timezone+.
    def to_time
      @to_time_with_timezone ||= getlocal(time_zone)
    end

    # So that +self+ <tt>acts_like?(:time)</tt>.
    def acts_like_time?
      true

    # Say we're a Time to thwart type checking.
    def is_a?(klass)
      klass == ::Time || super
    end
    alias_method :kind_of?, :is_a?

    # An instance of ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone is never blank
    def blank?
      false
    end

    def present? # :nodoc:
      true
    end

def bullet_for_li_node(node, index)
        if list_node_name_for_li_node(node) == "ol"
          "#{index + 1}."
        else
          "•"
        end
      def bullet_for_li_node(node)
        if list_node_name_for_li_node(node) == "ol"
          index = node.parent.elements.index(node)
          "#{index + 1}."
        else
          "•"
        end
      def plain_text_for_li_node(node, index)
        bullet = bullet_for_li_node(node, index)
        text = remove_trailing_newlines(plain_text_for_node_children(node))
        indentation = indentation_for_li_node(node)

        "#{indentation}#{bullet} #{text}\n"
      end

def serialize(attr_name, coder: nil, type: Object, comparable: false, yaml: {}, **options)
          coder ||= default_column_serializer
          unless coder
            raise ArgumentError, <<~MSG.squish
              missing keyword: :coder

              If no default coder is configured, a coder must be provided to `serialize`.
            MSG
          end

          column_serializer = build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml)

          attribute(attr_name, **options)

          decorate_attributes([attr_name]) do |attr_name, cast_type|
            if type_incompatible_with_serialize?(cast_type, coder, type)
              raise ColumnNotSerializableError.new(attr_name, cast_type)
            end

            cast_type = cast_type.subtype if Type::Serialized === cast_type
            Type::Serialized.new(cast_type, column_serializer, comparable: comparable)
          end
        end

        private
          def build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml = nil)
            # When ::JSON is used, force it to go through the Active Support JSON encoder
            # to ensure special objects (e.g. Active Record models) are dumped correctly
            # using the #as_json hook.

            if coder == ::JSON || coder == Coders::JSON
              coder = Coders::JSON.new
            end

            if coder == ::YAML || coder == Coders::YAMLColumn
              Coders::YAMLColumn.new(attr_name, type, **(yaml || {}))
            elsif coder.respond_to?(:new) && !coder.respond_to?(:load)
              coder.new(attr_name, type)
            elsif type && type != Object
              Coders::ColumnSerializer.new(attr_name, coder, type)
            else
              coder
            end
          end

          def type_incompatible_with_serialize?(cast_type, coder, type)
            cast_type.is_a?(ActiveRecord::Type::Json) && coder == ::JSON ||
              cast_type.respond_to?(:type_cast_array, true) && type == ::Array
          end
      end

## Rails 8.1.3.1 (July 29, 2026) ##

*   Disable libvips's unfuzzed image loaders and savers.

    libvips flags some of its loaders and savers as "unfuzzed" or "untrusted", meaning they are only
    safe for trusted content. Active Storage will call `Vips.block_untrusted(true)` to disable them
    while booting. An application that needs a specific loader or saver may re-enable it in an
    initializer.

    This is a breaking change for applications that process image types with an unfuzzed loader or
    saver. Variant transformation of BMP, ICO, and PSD attachments will raise `Vips::Error`, and
    analysis of these and other types such as SVG, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000, and Netpbm will no longer
    record `width` and `height`. Requesting an unfuzzed output format, typically FITS, JXL, or
    anything delegated to ImageMagick, will also raise `Vips::Error`. Attaching, storing, and
    downloading are unchanged.

    An application seeing `Vips::Error` raised during image transformation may wish to remove the
    affected content types from `config.active_storage.variable_content_types` in an initializer.
    Active Storage will then treat those attachments as not variable and will not generate variants
    for them. This most often matters to an application that transforms images during a request
    rather than in a background job, where the failure surfaces as an error response instead of a
    failed job.

    ```ruby
    Rails.application.config.active_storage.variable_content_types -=
      %w[ image/bmp image/vnd.microsoft.icon image/vnd.adobe.photoshop ]
    ```

    Applications using the `:mini_magick` variant processor will see no change in how their
    attachments are processed, but the loaders and savers will be disabled process-wide whenever
    ruby-vips is installed, and the version requirements below will still apply. Such an application
    may remove ruby-vips from its Gemfile to avoid both.

    The minimum supported version of libvips is now 8.13, and the minimum supported version of
    ruby-vips is now 2.2.1. These are the earliest versions that are capable of disabling untrusted
    operations. When ruby-vips is installed and either minimum is not met, Active Storage will raise
    a `RuntimeError` while booting rather than run in an unsecurable environment.

## Rails 8.1.2.1 (March 23, 2026) ##

*   Filter user supplied metadata in DirectUploadController

    [CVE-2026-33173]

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Configurable maxmimum streaming chunk size

    Makes sure that byte ranges for blobs don't exceed 100mb by default.
    Content ranges that are too big can result in denial of service.

    [CVE-2026-33174]

    *Gannon McGibbon*

*   Limit range requests to a single range

    [CVE-2026-33658]

    *Jean Boussier*


*   Prevent path traversal in `DiskService`.

    `DiskService#path_for` now raises an `InvalidKeyError` when passed keys with dot segments (".",
    ".."), or if the resolved path is outside the storage root directory.

    `#path_for` also now consistently raises `InvalidKeyError` if the key is invalid in any way, for
    example containing null bytes or having an incompatible encoding. Previously, the exception
    raised may have been `ArgumentError` or `Encoding::CompatibilityError`.

    `DiskController` now explicitly rescues `InvalidKeyError` with appropriate HTTP status codes.

    [CVE-2026-33195]

    *Mike Dalessio*

*   Prevent glob injection in `DiskService#delete_prefixed`.

    Escape glob metacharacters in the resolved path before passing to `Dir.glob`.

    Note that this change breaks any existing code that is relying on `delete_prefixed` to expand
    glob metacharacters. This change presumes that is unintended behavior (as other storage services
    do not respect these metacharacters).

## Rails 8.1.2 (January 08, 2026) ##

*   Restore ADC when signing URLs with IAM for GCS

    ADC was previously used for automatic authorization when signing URLs with IAM.
    Now it is again, but the auth client is memoized so that new credentials are only
    requested when the current ones expire. Other auth methods can now be used
    instead by setting the authorization on `ActiveStorage::Service::GCSService#iam_client`.

    ```ruby
    ActiveStorage::Blob.service.iam_client.authorization = Google::Auth::ImpersonatedServiceAccountCredentials.new(options)
    ```

    This is safer than setting `Google::Apis::RequestOptions.default.authorization`
    because it only applies to Active Storage and does not affect other Google API
    clients.

content.content:
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "sidekiq/job"

module Sidekiq
  class Rails < ::Rails::Engine
    class Reloader
      def initialize(app = ::Rails.application)
        @app = app
      end

      def call
        @app.reloader.wrap do
          yield
        end
      end

      def inspect
        "#<Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader @app=#{@app.class.name}>"
      end
    end

    # By including the Options module, we allow AJs to directly control sidekiq features
    # via the *sidekiq_options* class method and, for instance, not use AJ's retry system.
    # AJ retries don't show up in the Sidekiq UI Retries tab, save any error data, can't be
    # manually retried, don't automatically die, etc.
    #
    #   class SomeJob < ActiveJob::Base
    #     queue_as :default
    #     sidekiq_options retry: 3, backtrace: 10
    #     def perform
    #     end
    #   end
    initializer "sidekiq.active_job_integration" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        include ::Sidekiq::Job::Options unless respond_to?(:sidekiq_options)
      end
    end

    config.before_configuration do
      dep = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("7.0", "Sidekiq")
      dep.deprecate_methods(Sidekiq.singleton_class,
        default_worker_options: :default_job_options,
        "default_worker_options=": :default_job_options=)
    end

    # This hook happens after all initializers are run, just before returning
    # from config/environment.rb back to sidekiq/cli.rb.
    #
    # None of this matters on the client-side, only within the Sidekiq process itself.
    config.after_initialize do
      Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
        config[:reloader] = Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader.new

        # This is the integration code necessary so that if a job uses `Rails.logger.info "Hello"`,
        # it will appear in the Sidekiq console with all of the job context.
        unless ::Rails.logger == config.logger || ::ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(::Rails.logger, $stdout)
          if ::Rails::VERSION::STRING < "7.1"
            ::Rails.logger.extend(::ActiveSupport::Logger.broadcast(config.logger))
          else
            ::Rails.logger.broadcast_to(config.logger)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

def retry_on(*exceptions, wait: 3.seconds, attempts: 5, queue: nil, priority: nil, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT, report: false)
        rescue_from(*exceptions) do |error|
          executions = executions_for(exceptions)
          if attempts == :unlimited || executions < attempts
            ActiveSupport.error_reporter.report(error, source: "application.active_job") if report
            retry_job wait: determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm: wait, executions: executions, jitter: jitter), queue: queue, priority: priority, error: error
          else
            if block_given?
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error do
                yield self, error
              end
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
            else
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
              raise error
            end
          end
        end

# Rails 7.0.8.7 to 8.1.0 upgrade risk for Margin Notes

The upgrade spans four release series (7.1, 7.2, 8.0, 8.1). I found seven high-risk changes, six medium and about fifteen low. The most serious one breaks a data guarantee: a failed CSV import would start saving part of the batch instead of nothing.

The existing test suite would catch several of the high-risk changes, but not the Action Text plain-text change, the Astana time zone change, the cache expiry change, or the problem when old and new job workers run side by side.

I worked from the 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0 gem source, which I downloaded and unpacked into `/tmp/railsgems/src/{7.0.8.7,8.1.0}/`, the changelogs on the 7.1 to 8.1 stable branches, and a few pull requests. Each claim is tagged **[code]** (I read the 8.1.0 source), **[changelog]**, or **[inference]** (my reasoning, not verified). I did not run anything or change the application.

## Facts about the application the ratings depend on

Please correct any of these that are wrong.

- **Config defaults:** `config/application.rb:12` uses `config.load_defaults 7.0`. I assumed it stays at 7.0 for the upgrade. Raising it is a separate decision, covered below.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL only (`config/database.yml:18`). `citations` uses `doi` as its primary key and has no `id` column (`db/schema.rb:55`).
- **Jobs:** Active Job runs on Sidekiq 6.5.12 with the `redis` 4.8.1 gem (`config/application.rb:24`, `Gemfile`). Tests use the `:test` adapter. `ExportJob` is a plain Sidekiq job, not an Active Job.
  - Jobs are enqueued inside transactions and row locks (`citation.rb:15-23`, `note.rb:57-68`). The code relies on a failed enqueue raising an error.
  - `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` still defaults to `false` in 8.1 **[code]**, so this keeps working.
- **Cache:** none configured in production, so Rails falls back to its default file store at `tmp/cache` **[code]**. There is one fragment cache, in `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26`.
- **Rendering:** HTML through ERB, with Sprockets, importmap, Turbo and Action Text. The layout loads a vendored Trix 1.3.5 as a classic script (`layouts/application.html.erb:13`). `config/importmap.rb:8` pins `@rails/actiontext` to `actiontext.js`.
- **Time zones:** each reader has a time zone and the app depends on it in three places:
  - Reminder times use the reader's zone.
  - Digests deliberately follow the UTC day (described in `ARCHITECTURE.md`).
  - `next_day_reminder_at` deliberately keeps the reminder's UTC offset.
- **Secrets:** `config/secrets.yml` is read through `Rails.application.secrets` (`app/models/citation/provider.rb:13`).
- **Tests:** `config/environments/test.rb:31` sets `show_exceptions = false`, and several tests use `assert_raises` against requests.
- **Deployment:** I assumed a rolling deploy is possible, meaning web and worker processes on different Rails versions share one Redis queue for a while.

## High risk

### 1. Leaving a transaction with `return` now commits instead of rolling back
- **Before:** in 7.0, exiting a `transaction` block with `return` after a write rolled the transaction back **[code]** (`transaction.rb:336-342` in 7.0).
- **Now:** 7.2 removed that behavior. In 8.1 the block commits whenever no exception is raised **[code]** (`transaction.rb:643-677`).
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:53-58`. `Import#apply` runs `save!` and then `return false unless row.note.save` inside `transaction do`.
- **What goes wrong:** when a later row fails to save, the import record, the earlier rows' notes, and any new citations they autosaved are all committed. `ARCHITECTURE.md` promises "nothing from the batch remains".
  - `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:48-73` would catch this.
  - The fix is to raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, or to return after the block.
- **Source:** [7-2-stable activerecord CHANGELOG](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md) ("Remove deprecated behavior that would rollback a transaction block when exited using `return`..."), and [PR #48600](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48600).

### 2. `DigestJob` now receives the request time in the reader's zone
- **Before:** 7.0 deserialized a TimeWithZone argument in the worker's zone (UTC) **[code]**.
- **Now:** since 7.1.3/7.2, the serializer stores `time_zone` and restores it on deserialization **[code]** (`activejob/lib/active_job/serializers/time_with_zone_serializer.rb`).
- **Where:** `app/models/user.rb:35,41` passes `Time.current.in_time_zone(time_zone)`. `app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9` then uses `requested_at.to_date` and `requested_at.all_day`.
- **What goes wrong:** the digest's date and its "notes updated that day" window become the reader's local day. The Redis reservation key is still the UTC date (`user.rb:36`).
  - Near local midnight, readers get the wrong day's notes and the wrong date in the subject line, with no error.
  - `test/controllers/digests_controller_test.rb:33` would catch the date change.
- **Source:** [PR #50240](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/50240), and the 7-1-stable / 7-2-stable activejob changelogs.

### 3. `DigestJob`'s BigDecimal argument changes format, which breaks old workers during a mixed-version deploy
- **Before:** 7.0 passed a BigDecimal through as-is, and Sidekiq stored it as a string.
- **Now:** 7.2 removed that primitive path. 8.1 always wraps it as `{"_aj_serialized" => "ActiveJob::Serializers::BigDecimalSerializer", ...}` **[code]** **[changelog]**.
- **Where:** `user.rb:41` (`reading_completion`) and `digest_mailer.rb:10`. `BigDecimal(BigDecimal)` still works, so 8.1 on both sides is fine **[inference]**.
- **What goes wrong:** a 7.0 worker cannot look up that serializer class. It raises `ArgumentError`, which surfaces as `DeserializationError` **[code]** (7.0 `serializers.rb:42-43`).
  - Digest jobs enqueued by 8.1 web processes fail and are retried by Sidekiq until the workers are upgraded.
  - The reverse direction (7.0 payload read by an 8.1 worker) works.
  - The tests won't catch this. Upgrade workers first, or drain the queue.
- **Source:** [7-2-stable activejob CHANGELOG](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md) ("Remove deprecated primitive serializer for `BigDecimal` arguments").

### 4. `TimeWithZone#to_time` now keeps the zone instead of the fixed offset
- **Before:** with 7.0 defaults, `getlocal(utc_offset)` returned a fixed offset, so adding 86,400 seconds kept the old offset across a daylight saving change.
- **Now:** 8.1 always uses `getlocal(time_zone)` **[code]** (`time_with_zone.rb:497-499`).
- **Where:** `app/models/note.rb:43-45` (`reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`), shown in `app/views/notes/_reminder.html.erb:19`.
- **What goes wrong:** across a daylight saving change, the "24 hours later" preview shows a different offset and clock time than today.
  - The instant is the same, and `postpone_reminder` uses `.to_i`, so the postponed reminder itself is unaffected **[inference]**.
  - `test/controllers/reminders_controller_test.rb:21` (expects `-04:00`) and `ARCHITECTURE.md` document the old behavior. The test would catch it.
- **Source:** [8.1.0 activesupport CHANGELOG](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md) ("Remove deprecated support for `to_time` to preserve the system local time"), and the 8-0-stable entry adding `:zone`.

### 5. The "Astana" time zone now maps to Asia/Almaty instead of Asia/Dhaka
- **What changed:** `ActiveSupport::TimeZone::MAPPING` diff **[code]**. Almaty is UTC+5 on current tzdata, Dhaka is UTC+6 **[inference]**.
- **Where:** stored `users.time_zone`, used by `user.rb:22` (`local_time`), `note.rb:37` (`reminder_at`), and the reminder views and email.
- **What goes wrong:** for readers set to "Astana", reminder times are displayed an hour off, and new reminders entered as local times map to different instants. There is no error and no test covers it.
- **Smaller mapping changes:** "Greenland" now maps to America/Nuuk and "Canberra" to Australia/Canberra. These are renames or aliases with the same rules **[inference]**. "Asuncion" is a new choice.
- **Source:** [PR #51317](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/51317).

### 6. Action Text `to_plain_text` output changed
- **Before / now:** two differences **[code]**, from a diff of `actiontext/lib/action_text/plain_text_conversion.rb`. I found no changelog entry for them.
  - Ordered-list numbers now count element siblings only. In 7.0 they counted all child nodes, so whitespace between `<li>` tags inflated the numbers.
  - The contents of `<script>` and `<style>` are now dropped.
- **Where:**
  - Markdown exports: `app/models/export.rb:78`.
  - Note list previews: `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:53`.
  - Import previews: `app/views/imports/preview.html.erb:58`.
  - Imported `body_html` is stored unsanitized, so it can contain both of these.
- **What goes wrong:** exported files and previews for the same notes differ from today's output, with no error. No test covers lists or style tags.

### 7. A negative cache `expires_in` now means the fragment never expires
- **Before:** in 7.0 the entry was written already expired, so it was never served **[code]**.
- **Now:** in 8.1 the negative `expires_in` is deleted and an `ArgumentError` is logged and reported, so the entry is written with no expiry **[code]** (`cache.rb:922-924,937-945`). Raising instead requires 7.1 defaults.
- **Where:** `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26` passes `expires_in: export.expires_at - Time.current`, which is negative once an export has expired.
- **What goes wrong:** "Expired" fragments stay in the file store permanently, and each one logs an error when written. The content stays correct, so the practical impact is low **[inference]**. No test catches it.
- **Source:** [PR #45892](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/45892).

## Medium risk

### 1. `Rails.application.secrets` was removed in 7.2
- **Before:** deprecated in 7.1 **[changelog]**. In 8.1 the method no longer exists **[code]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/citation/provider.rb:13`, the default argument, and `config/secrets.yml`.
- **What goes wrong:** citation enrichment fails at runtime, not at boot. Any test that runs the job would catch it.
- **Decision needed:** where these settings should live: credentials, `config_for`, or plain ENV. `ARCHITECTURE.md` also documents this setup.
- **Source:** [7-2-stable railties CHANGELOG](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/railties/CHANGELOG.md).

### 2. `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` now defaults to `nil`
- **Before:** in 7.0 it was pre-filled with the sanitizer's tags plus `action-text-attachment`, `figure` and `figcaption`.
- **Now:** since 7.1 it is `nil`, and the defaults are computed at render time in `sanitizer_allowed_tags` **[code]**.
- **Where:** `config/initializers/action_text.rb:3` uses `+=`, which becomes `nil + Array` and fails at boot.
- **Trap:** the obvious fix, `allowed_tags = %w[details summary]`, would silently strip every other tag from rendered notes. The fix needs to rebuild the full default list.
- **Source:** [7-1-stable actiontext CHANGELOG](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) (HTML5 sanitizer entry).

### 3. `show_exceptions = false` now behaves like `:all`
- **Before:** `false` meant exceptions were raised in tests.
- **Now:** support for booleans was removed in 7.2. `ExceptionWrapper#show?` falls through to `true` for anything that isn't `:none` or `:rescuable` **[code]**.
- **Where:** `config/environments/test.rb:31`.
- **What goes wrong:** tests silently get error pages instead of exceptions. `assert_raises` tests break, for example `digests_controller_test.rb:51` and `exports_controller_test.rb:126-127`, and other failures can be hidden behind error-page responses.
- **Decision needed:** `:none` keeps today's behavior. `:rescuable` is the new generator default.
- **Source:** [7-1-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/actionpack/CHANGELOG.md) and 7-2-stable actionpack changelogs.

### 4. The built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated and will be removed in 8.2
- **What changed:** 8.1 logs a deprecation warning when `queue_adapter = :sidekiq` is set **[code]** (`sidekiq_adapter.rb:33`).
- **Where:** `config/application.rb:24`.
- **Decision needed:** the replacement is Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later, which ships its own adapter. That upgrade moves Sidekiq from the `redis` gem to `redis-client`, which affects:
  - the direct `Sidekiq.redis { |r| r.sadd/expire/srem }` calls in `user.rb:38-43`;
  - `rescue Redis::BaseError` in `notebook.rb:28`.
- **Compatibility note:** Sidekiq 6.5.12's Rails integration already handles the 7.1 logger API, so it works with 8.1 for now **[code]**. Its `rack ~> 2.0` constraint keeps Rack on 2.2, which 8.1 allows **[code]**.
- **Source:** [PR #53058](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53058).

### 5. Trix moved to version 2 in a separate gem
- **What changed:**
  - Action Text 7.1 moved to Trix 2 **[changelog]**. 8.1 depends on the `action_text-trix ~> 2.1.15` gem **[code]**.
  - `actiontext.js` is now a UMD bundle, with a separate `actiontext.esm.js` **[code]**.
- **Where:**
  - `*= require trix` in `app/assets/stylesheets/actiontext.css:6` will now resolve to the Trix 2.1.15 stylesheet, while the JavaScript is still the vendored Trix 1.3.5 (`layouts/application.html.erb:13`).
  - `config/importmap.rb:8` imports the UMD file. It probably still works through `globalThis` **[inference]**.
  - Upload errors now show an `alert` where 7.0 threw an exception **[code]**.
- **Decision needed:** adopt the bundled Trix 2 and drop the vendored copy, or vendor the Trix 1 stylesheet and pin `actiontext.esm.js`. This needs a check in the browser.

### 6. Whether to raise `load_defaults` later
Staying at 7.0 works. Each step up changes behavior this app depends on **[code]** (`railties/lib/rails/application/configuration.rb`):
- **7.1:**
  - `default_column_serializer = nil` makes `serialize :preferences` (`notebook.rb:7`) fail.
  - `raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly` makes notebook updates fail, because the form resubmits the slug (`notebooks/_form.html.erb:13`, `notebook.rb:8`).
  - `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time` makes the expired export page raise (high-risk item 7).
- **7.2:** `postgresql_adapter_decode_dates` returns `Date` objects, so `Date.iso8601(day)` in `notebook.rb:40` fails.
- **8.0:** `strict_freshness` changes how conditional GETs are evaluated (`export_downloads_controller.rb:11`).

## Low risk (mechanical; booting or the existing tests would catch these)

- `retry_on ... wait: :exponentially_longer` (`app/jobs/citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`): removed in 7.2, so the retry handler raises "Couldn't determine a delay" **[code]**.
  - If missed, the citation would stay pending through Sidekiq's own retries.
  - Rename to `:polynomially_longer` (same formula). `citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:60` catches it.
- `set(wait_until: reminder_epoch)` with an Integer (`note.rb:61`): numeric `scheduled_at` was removed in 7.2, and `serialize` calls `Integer#utc`. Pass `Time.at(...)` instead **[code]**.
- `enum status: {...}, _prefix: true` (`note.rb:10`): the keyword form was removed in 8.0. Use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true` **[changelog]** **[code]**.
- `serialize :tags, JSON` (`note.rb:12`): the positional coder was removed in 7.2. Use `coder: JSON` **[code]**.
- `alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color` (`note.rb:14`): `color` comes from `store_accessor`, not a column, and aliasing non-attributes now raises `ArgumentError`. Use `alias_method` for the reader and the writer **[code]**.
- `citation[:id]` (`import.rb:68`): no longer maps to the `doi` primary key (removed in 7.2) and raises `MissingAttributeError`. Use `citation.id` or `citation.doi` **[code]**.
- `form_with(model: nil, ...)` (`notes/index.html.erb:12`): raises `ArgumentError` since 8.0. Drop `model: nil` **[code]**.
- `get "/notes", "/journal", to:` (`config/routes.rb:18`): multiple paths raise `ArgumentError` in 8.1 ([PR #52409](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/52409) deprecated it in 8.0). Split into two routes **[code]**.
- `fragments.sum` on strings (`export.rb:42`): Active Support's `Enumerable#sum` override was removed in 7.1, so this raises `TypeError`. Use `join` **[code]**. Export tests catch it.
- The JSON column coder now writes `<`, `>` and `&` unescaped in `tags` (`note.rb:12`). The decoded values are identical and both versions read both forms **[code]**.
- `Note.connection` (`notebook.rb:40`): soft-deprecated, with no warning by default **[code]**.
- `form.rich_text_area` (`notes/_form.html.erb:50`): now a plain alias of `rich_textarea`.
- Development and test `secret_key_base` now comes from `tmp/local_secret.txt` (or credentials) instead of `tmp/development_secret.txt` **[code]**. This invalidates development sessions and signed IDs in existing development data only. Production uses credentials or ENV as before.
- The `concurrent-ruby 1.3.4` and `minitest ~> 5.25` Gemfile pins still satisfy 8.1's requirements and can be revisited later.

## Judged not relevant

- **MySQL, SQLite, Trilogy and composite primary keys:** PostgreSQL only.
- **`enqueue_after_transaction_commit`:** still `false` by default in 8.1, and the app never sets it.
- **Action Cable:** no channels. The production Redis adapter accepts `redis` 4.
- **Action Mailbox:** loaded by `rails/all` but unused.
- **Active Storage variants, previews, libvips, S3, GCS and Azure:** no image processor and Disk service only.
- **JSON rendering changes** (escaping, `escape_json_responses`): the app serves no JSON.
- **Rack 3 and `:unprocessable_entity`:** Sidekiq 6.5 keeps Rack on 2.2.
- **Cache format:** the 7.0 format is still supported.
- **Built-in locales:** only gained keys. The `:long` and `:short` formats the app uses are unchanged.
- **`TimeZone#iso8601` and `#at`:** unchanged.
- **Pessimistic locking:** only a read-only guard was added.
- **Migrations:** the `[5.2]`, `[6.0]` and `[7.0]` versions are still supported.
- **Strict freshness and `default_headers`:** only change with newer `load_defaults`.

## One more consideration: 8.1.0 is not the latest 8.1 patch

8.1.0 lacks security fixes released afterwards in 8.1.2.1 and 8.1.3.1 **[changelog]**, several in parts this app uses:
- Active Storage Disk service path traversal and glob injection;
- metadata filtering in the direct-upload controller (open to anonymous users here);
- range-request limits;
- `NumberConverter`, which `number_to_human_size` and `number_to_percentage` use;
- `SafeBuffer#%` and the tag helpers.

Consider targeting the latest 8.1.x instead.
